strengths: Comprehensive and well-designed benchmark (VLMBias) with 1,392 counterfeitual images across 7 diverse domains and systematic modifications
Thorough empirical evaluation with multiple ablations, sanity checks, background removal experiments, and human baselines
Clear presentation of failure modes with effective visualizations and systematic documentation across multiple VLMs
Actionable diagnostic insight that background removal significantly improves performance (from 17% to ~40%)
Well-controlled experiments with repeated runs and cross-domain validation
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: Core insight that VLMs rely on prior knowledge over visual information is well-established in existing literature on VLM hallucinations and biases
No meaningful solutions proposed: Paper is purely diagnostic without proposing architectural changes, training methods, or practical remedies beyond background removal (which is often impractical)
Artificial and limited task scope: Simple counting/identification tasks with unclear relevance to real-world VLM applications
Shallow mechanistic analysis: Shows THAT biases exist but not WHY; lacks investigation of attention patterns, internal representations, or decision-making processes
Statistical rigor concerns: Most results lack confidence intervals or significance tests despite extensive testing; human study has small sample size (n=78)
Image generation bias: Acknowledged limitation that modifications are generated with specific tools (Gemini, GPT-4o) which may introduce their own biases
Limited practical impact: Does not provide actionable guidance for practitioners, users, or researchers on how to address identified biases
Incomplete baseline comparisons: Limited comparison with specialized models and missing ablations on model components that contribute to bias

strengths: Comprehensive and well-designed benchmark (VLMBias) with 1,392 counteractual images across 7 diverse domains, systematically created with rigorous quality control
Thorough experimental evaluation spanning 5 SOTA VLMs with multiple ablations (background removal, reasoning tokens, few-shot learning, tool access) that systematically characterize failure modes
Rigorous methodology including sanity checks, human study validation with 78 participants reaching 96.88% accuracy, and multiple resolution testing
Clear, quantified findings with important practical implications (e.g., 75.70% bias rate on counteractual images, +21.09 accuracy gain from background removal)
Excellent reproducibility with extensive appendices documenting task design, prompts, data generation pipelines, and promised code/data release
Significant practical relevance for understanding VLM limitations and implications for safety-critical deployments
Well-organized presentation with effective visualizations and logical flow from problem identification through systematic characterization
weaknesses: Core finding that VLMs rely on prior knowledge over visual evidence is somewhat expected and builds incrementally on prior bias literature rather than presenting novel insights
Limited mechanistic analysis of why failures occur; paper is primarily empirical documentation of failures rather than investigation of underlying causes in vision encoders or reasoning stages
Minimal exploration of mitigation strategies; while problems are well-characterized, concrete solutions or guidance for model improvement are largely absent
Narrow evaluation scope: only 5 VLMs tested; missing comparisons with non-VLM baselines or models specialized for counting/visual reasoning tasks
Statistical rigor could be improved: limited confidence intervals, significance testing, or prediction uncertainty estimates provided; variation across runs noted but not fully quantified
Human study is modest in scale (78 participants) and uses somewhat artificial time-pressure conditions (0.2-2s exposure); limited exploration of alternative evaluation protocols
Paper density and length (73 pages) with substantial appendices makes the contribution somewhat difficult to synthesize; some redundancy could be condensed
